professions.name: Mining
professions.taught: You hang the pick at your belt. You can now mine.
professions.description: Ore lies in seams along the cliffs and on cave floors. It takes a pick and a strong back, and any smith will pay for what you carry out.

professions.name: Woodcutting
professions.taught: You hang the hatchet at your belt. You can now cut timber.
professions.description: Wind-felled timber is anyone's to cut. It takes a hatchet. Standing trees are left to stand. A woodcutter who knows the grain whittles bows and staves too, at a bench or by a fire.

professions.name: Herbalism
professions.description: Bare hands and a good eye. Herbs grow where the ground suits them, and grow back when picked.

professions.name: Cooking
professions.description: Meat, flour and eggs become something worth eating at any fire: an inn's hearth, a bake oven, a cookfire. Everyone can cook. Few do it well.

professions.name: Blacksmithing
professions.description: Ore to bars, and bars to blades and plate, at a forge. A craft takes years, and a body has time for three.
professions.learnAt: Taken up at a forge: Vell's smithy in Oakhaven, the field anvil on the Peaks pass, Oska's bone-anvil on the Ashland Rim, Alder-Knot's ember-stone on the Verdant Shore. A blacksmith will start you off wherever you find one.
professions.takeUp: You look over the anvil, the tongs and the quench tub, and begin.

trainerLines.text: Mind the scale. Copper first; it forgives you.
Bone teaches patience. Iron teaches the rest. Strike where it glows, not where you wish it did.
Metal is only stone that has been listened to. Listen first, flesh-folk. Then strike.
Hammer, tongs and a steady arm. The rest is burns and practice.

helpLines.text: Pump it slow. Let the coals do the work.
More air. Bone or iron, the fire wants feeding.
Breathe with the fire. It is older than both of us.
Here, I'll keep the fire up for you.

professions.name: Simpling
professions.description: Herbs to simples at a herbalist's bench: draughts that heal or fill what a body spends, tinctures and cordials that strengthen for half an hour, salves that harden the skin, and a draught that lifts poisons and bleeds. The village's simples, not the Council's alchemy. A craft takes years, and a body has time for three.
professions.learnAt: Taken up at a herbalist's bench: Lisbet's drying hut in Oakhaven, Wenna Coyle's bench in Khaven, Mother Vane's salt-bench on the Ashland Rim, Moss-Lantern's bench on the Verdant Shore. A herbalist will start you off wherever you find one.
professions.takeUp: You look over the jars, the mortar and the little still, and begin.
professions.helping: {name} keeps the still at a simmer for you.

trainerLines.text: Never boil yarrow. Warm it, and wait. Start with that and you'll do.
Gloves for the cap, and don't breathe over the pot. Khaven buries enough as it is.
Clean vials and a slow fire. The herbs tell you the rest, if you listen.

helpLines.text: Stir it the other way. Don't ask me why. It works.
Slowly. A draught won't be hurried.

professions.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (the books' alchemy is the Council's industry; the village's simpling is not it)

professions.name: Leatherworking
professions.description: Hides to jerkins, gloves, leggings and boots: salted, tanned with bark and stitched, at a bench or by a fire. The hides come off what you hunt. A craft takes years, and a body has time for three.
professions.learnAt: Taken up at a herbalist's bench or by any fire, or from a leatherworker: Maud Tanner in Oakhaven will start you off.
professions.takeUp: You lay out the awl, the waxed thread and the fleshing knife, and begin.
professions.helping: {name} holds the hide taut for you.

trainerLines.text: Salt it the day you skin it, or don't bother skinning it. Then we'll talk.
Sharp awl, waxed thread, and never cut toward yourself.

helpLines.text: Pull it flat. Flatter. Leather remembers every crease.
Here, I'll hold the edge while you stitch.

professions.name: Weaving
professions.description: Fleece to yarn and yarn to cloth: hoods, mantles, robes and breeches, dyed with what grows in each zone, by a fire or at a bench. The stalls sell the folds' fleeces. A craft takes years, and a body has time for three.
professions.learnAt: Taken up by any fire or at a herbalist's bench, or from a shepherd: the folds above Oakhaven and on the Peaks.
professions.takeUp: You card a fleece, set the spindle turning, and begin.
professions.helping: {name} cards the wool while you spin.

trainerLines.text: Spin it fine and even. A lumpy yarn makes a lumpy hood, and everyone will know.

helpLines.text: I'll card, you spin. We'll be done by dark.
